game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
My intention was to write this review after completing the fifth and final chapter after its release. Now that I've completed the game, I feel that I can give this game the review that it deserves. 

I was very, very surprised with how well this game was executed. I've never come across a game quite like this. Orwell is a game where you play as an investigator who is trying to discover the person behind a crime by ruffling through relevant internet posts as well as phone calls, emails, etc. You then send information you deem as relevant to your advisor, who then decides what to do with said information. As I was playing this game, I really felt the pressure on what kind of narrative I was showing to the government and the policeforce regarding the people I was investigating, which is why I believe this game is so brilliant. You really feel the need to think carefully about what things you send out because there is no taking back what you submit once it's out there, which I believe is one of the underlying messages of the game's story. 

I would liken this game to an interactive choose-your-own adventure. Regarding the gameplay, it does not involve much other than reading through files and articles, and clicking to drag data of your choice into the government's database. Certain pieces of information will unlock more articles and files for you to read through. That being said, while I was playing the game these simple mechanics actually helped me stay more immersed in the story. They were uncomplicated and helped my attention stay focused on my "job" and the impact I was having. If your idea of a good game involves more gameplay elements than this, I would not recommend it to you, but if you really enjoy a good story, then please consider giving this game a try. 

Where this game really thrives, I believe, is its attention to detail. The writing in this game is fantastic, as well as the music. The music is mainly ambient, but when you come across important information the music changes dramatically to match the feeling of what you have discovered. The writing paired with the music really kept me at the edge of my seat throughout each episode. I really enjoyed how versatile the writing was as well. The writers managed to create incredibly in-depth characters that each felt very real with their own motives and personalities. At times I felt obligated to protect these people or felt awful about info I might have uploaded about them if it turned out I was incorrect. Without spoiling anything, the writing really makes you think about how people generally show many different aspects of themselves to different people, and as the investigator you have to decipher which "mask" is the way that person really feels or thinks. 

Unfortunately for people who buy the game at this point, you will not be getting the weekly emails to report back to duty  because all five episodes have already been released. These emails really helped me stay immersed in the universe of the game and I really felt like I was reporting back to duty for a job, and I commend the developers for these small touches that added to my immersion in the game. Even though players who buy the game now have access to all episodes at once, I would really recommend taking a break of a day between each episode if you can. I really think it will help you stay immersed in the world. 

Honestly, if you enjoy dystopian stories like 1984 and want to experience an innovative way of playing, you will really enjoy this game. I hope that many people give this game a chance because it will really make you question government security and the things that you post publicly online. I'm going to keep an eye out for more games by these developers because I feel that they are really creating a new, innovative market and I am really excited to see what else they can bring to the gaming industry. 

I give this game a 10/10

game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
I wish I could give this a rating... Like "B+" or "70%".     

I came here having tried Orwell a few years ago and didn't take to it... Then I played "Return of the Obra Dinn" and was so entranced by it I searched for "Game like..." and this came up, so I went back and started over.

I'll just say that this game is NOTHING like "Return of the Obra Dinn".    It feels like the "Walking Simulator" of detective games. You don't 'detect' so to speak, more than you just walk through scads and scads of documents and photographs, and picking out important pieces that are pre-highlighted for you.  Occasionally you get to make a moral / ambiguous choice between two things with far too little / ambiguous information.   This is kind of the point of the game... To show how easily we can be led down a path of conclusion based on scant evidence... Is the player 'aware' enough of the situation to select the correct interpretation.  Sometimes it's easy, sometimes it's not.

Where Orwell falls down is that the consequence of what you pull out of the documentation isn't always clear.   You can be pulling out loads of stuff, with the occasional snide / snippy remark from your 'advisor', with no noticeable progress in the game.  Then all of a sudden, you pick something and *BOOM*  the whole world spins on its axis, and you suddenly get more context, albeit too late.

Now, as I said, the 'late information binding' thang is the whole Orwell shtick, but it's really s****g annoying when you're playing.  It's only in the end game, that the whole POINT of the game becomes clear and you realise that the annoyance you're feeling has a purpose.

Then the game offers you a moral choice...   Carry on, or rebel.  For me, the decision was pretty clear cut, but it didn't look like it had much effect, tbh.     And that's the other big issue, is that you're never sure if you chose correctly, wrongly, or your choice made no major difference.  Some might say this adds 'replayability', but to be honest, I don't think I can be bothered clicking through dozens of semi-meaningless PDFs for another 10 hours to choose different outcomes to test the theory....


I kinda enjoyed playing Orwell... But there were times when I just wanted the story to advance, but it simply refused because I had to make a choice.   And by this point, there was so little context, and so much cruft to wade through, I gave up and just picked one option to make the game carry on.   Perhaps that was the point as well.. I dunno. It's midnight and my brain hurts from reading all this text on the screen.

It's under a tenner on Steam right now. I can't remember how I got Orwell, but if I paid over £10, I don't think I got a good price/enjoyment ratio.    It's a relatively solid game, and has a fair point to make on the way the surveillance state is going, and had great music, good visuals and an interesting setting.  Get it if you like making your own deductions and choices.
